item_01.why_target: Two disjoint set systems can be two-coloured independently and optimally, so the discrepancy of the union is just the larger of the two.
item_01.why_bound: With n additive and m/n essentially preserved, sqrt(n log(m/n)) squares add: B(I1 u I2)^2 = B1^2 + B2^2.

item_02.why_target: Amplification multiplying size by a bounded factor per step keeps size linear, so sizes add.
item_02.why_bound: Raising size to the k-th power is exactly size(I1 (x) I2) = size(I1)*size(I2).

item_03.why_target: CFGS give Delta = ceil(n^{1/2}) and n adds, so Delta^2 adds.
item_03.why_bound: log(n1+n2) = max(log n1, log n2) + O(1), so the counting board obeys a max law rather than l2.

item_04.why_target: A cap times a cap is a cap in the sum of dimensions, so |A| multiplies as n adds.
item_04.why_bound: Each density-increment step costs one dimension, so the saving accumulated is linear in n (a polynomial factor), an additive-scale mechanism.

item_05.why_target: (1-eps^2)^{O(k)} is exponential decay in k, so values multiply across coordinates.
item_05.why_bound: (1-eps^3)^{Omega(k)} is itself a k-th power; only the constant in the exponent differs.

item_06.why_target: val(G^2) > val(G)^2 because provers correlate; submultiplicative but not any of these laws.
item_06.why_bound: val(G^k) = val(G)^k is by definition the multiplicative law.

item_07.why_target: Larsen-Nelson is Omega(eps^{-2} log n) and log n is additive, so dimensions add.
item_07.why_bound: O(log n / eps^2) with log n additive gives m(P1 (x) P2) = m(P1) + m(P2).

item_08.why_target: Theta is a limit of alpha(G^{box k})^{1/k}, so capacity multiplies by construction; alpha itself is only supermultiplicative.
item_08.why_bound: alpha*(G box H) = alpha*(G) alpha*(H) exactly, so the bound tensors; it is just not tight.

item_09.why_target: For a direct sum the largest root is the largest among the blocks, so flat in block count.
item_09.why_bound: The tr exp factor costs only log of the block count, so the requirement shifts by an O(log) drift rather than a sum: essentially the max law with a logarithmic loss.

item_10.why_target: The tensor of a product instance is the tensor product, so complexity multiplies.
item_10.why_bound: Border rank is submultiplicative under tensor product, so the bound respects the same law.

item_11.why_target: CFGS give ceil(n^{1/2}) and n adds, so squares add.
item_11.why_bound: A^2 = nI makes the eigenvalue sqrt(n), and sqrt(n1+n2) = sqrt(sqrt(n1)^2 + sqrt(n2)^2).

item_12.why_target: The product of two set systems has |S1|*|S2| sets while VC dimension adds.
item_12.why_bound: sum_{i<=d} C(n,i) ~ n^d is exponential in d, and with d additive n^{d1+d2} = n^{d1} n^{d2}.

item_13.why_target: Independent sets in strong powers compose and the capacity limit multiplies.
item_13.why_bound: theta(G box H) = theta(G) theta(H) exactly; only its value is loose.

item_14.why_target: A net for a product must handle heavy ranges from both components and scales linearly in VC dimension, which adds.
item_14.why_bound: O((d/eps) log(1/eps)) is linear in d, which is additive, so the bound for the product is the sum.
